newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's BHP in management crisis.
newsitem.headline: Australia's BHP in management crisis.

text.p: Australian resource giant Broken Hill Pty Ltd (BHP) lost its third senior executive in as many days on Friday, ending three days of management turmoil which wiped about A$2.0 billion (US$1.5 billion) off its market value.

News of the latest departure from Australia's biggest listed company came shortly before the close of trading on Friday and sent the group's already shaky share price tumbling and forced the Australian stock market to a lower close.

BHP closed 45 cents lower at A$16.99 and the All Ordinaries index, which looked as if it would close fairly steady, lost 9.4 points to 2,717.7. The steel, oil and mining giant now has a capitalisation of A$34 billion.
BHP said on Friday its petroleum chief executive, John O'Connor, had resigned due to irreconcilable differences with the board, but the company's statement to the market gave no more details.
The surprise announcement came as investors were already nervous over the sudden departures of minerals division chief Dick Carter and iron ore boss Geoff Wedlock over the previous two days.
O'Connor jumped ship after he was reported in local newspapers as having argued for the floating off of BHP's petroleum division, the biggest contributor to group earnings.
A float is believed to have been rejected by the board.
